newsitem.title: USA: Excite sets pact to launch free e-mail.
newsitem.headline: Excite sets pact to launch free e-mail.

text.p: Excite Inc. said Sunday it plans to offer free Web-based e-mail in conjunction with a closely held e-mail company backed by the Rockefeller family.

Terms of the deal with the company, Whowhere Inc., were not disclosed. But officials said the agreement would make Excite the first Internet search company to offer free e-mail. Several other companies specialize in offering computer users e-mail via the World Wide Web but do not provide Internet searches.
Officials of Whowhere said the deal was the first of several expected in its e-mail offerings.
Excite's e-mail service will compete with privately held Hotmail Corp., which now says it has more than 5 million subscribers, along with Bigfoot and Rocketmail, a unit of Four11 Corp.
The service, which is advertising supported, will allow Web users to pick up e-mail over the Internet using a standard browser without being tied to a specific computer, officials said.

Joe Kraus, co-founder and senior vice president of Excite, based in Redwood City, Calif., said the service was another addition to the company's effort to make Excite people's home base on the Internet.
Internet watchers said Excite's deal puts it a step closer to offering Internet services similar to those from online services such as America Online Inc, which owns a minority stake in Excite.

Companies involved in offering e-mail addresses, which are generally supported by adertising, have been gearing up for a battle for customers. Last week, Acxiom Corp. said it was buying a stake in Bigfoot and set an alliance combining Bigfoot's e-mail service with Acxiom's marketing databases.
Whowhere has a directory of 11 million personal e-mail addresses, 80 million U.S. residential phone numbers and addresses and 800,000 listings of personal pages on the Web.
Dale Fuller, the former Apple Computer Inc. executive who became chief executive of Whowhere in May, said the deal with Excite could be worth $2 million to $10 million a year to his company.
Selling e-mail through third parties is new for Whowhere, which competes in the directory market with Internet companies like Four11, InfoSpace, Bigbook and others.
Last month, Whowhere set a partnership with American School Directory to provide free Web-based e-mail to students.
Whowhere is backed by $4 million in venture capital from Venrock, the Rockefeller family's venture capital arm, and is considering making an initial public offering, Fuller said.
